Continuity on the unit sphere times the finitely many fixed-base unit balls gives the needed uniform linear lower bound. Testing the constraint at u=X/|X| then bounds all feasible X for small t. The constraints are closed and convex for t≥0.

On a common ball a uniform field bound L yields support excess at most tL. If the old inball has center o and radius r, the inward homothet with ratio 1−tL/r has support margin at least tL in every direction. The old parallel body is contained in the outer homothet with ratio 1+tL/r about o, by the same support inequality. These give positivity, Hausdorff control and the uniform signed fractional radial bound.

Jensen at any anchored convex combination gives u·ΣλX_z+tΦ(u,p,ΣλX_z)≤Σλh_z(u)≤h_p(u), exactly the new defining inequality. Grouping representations by sampled base gives each new actual fiber, and completeness excludes new integer sites.

At a new radial endpoint, joint continuity and compactness of the unit sphere ensure an active constraint, since uniform strict slack would give an interior neighborhood. The old normal gives the lower bound on s_t/t. The active new constraint gives the upper bound once its scalar radial denominator is positive. Its limiting support gap is zero by the O(t) radial bound, so regularity makes its normal converge to the old normal and the denominator tends to a number at least the old inradius. This squeeze permits either sign. Convex boundaries have regular normals surface-almost everywhere; in d=1 both endpoints are regular with counting measure.

Nonnegative finite sums preserve the assumed convexity and continuity and yield the sum of the signed speeds. Both signs of a normal-dependent affine field are affine. In particular Φ=−u·b gives exactly the common translation K_z+tb and signed inward speed −n·b. Independent cap normals with nonzero old continuous part stay admissible for small t, and the positive exponential scale has the requested logarithmic derivative.
